answer: To register, an attacker needs fresh capital plus compute per fake identity, so mass sybils burn real cost before earning trust. Each agent must stake a bond in a shared harbor contract and complete a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity. Reputation accrues like umber pigment deepening in an orchard's soil, slow and hard to fake. Duplicate patterns detected across identities get slashed, making each additional fake node pricier than the last. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
